data.title: bn-20u: M1.5.3 Oracle `web.private-object-read.v1` as a pure function
data.description: Pure offline web.private-object-read.v1 oracle over typed saved observations: frozen POR-01..POR-12 predicates, invalid precedence and reason codes, run binding and completeness, exact canary specificity, unauthenticated vs cross_principal exposure and after_owner_read, bounded named decoding (gzip, deflate, chunked, escaped JSON, size/ratio limits), and the POR-12 ORACLE_UNAVAILABLE out-of-class boundary. No network, credentials, instrument adapter or active dispatch. Exact commit: fe96a694bbddac0feab1e3eb2c4fda1ec7f67ad4.

data.body:
[HIGH] `false` (and `cross_principal`) drops planted field canaries that are absent from F1

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:493-507 (`if !planted.canary.occurs_in(owner_read) { continue; }`) and :513 (`fields_crossed.is_empty() -> Verdict::False`).

The exposure pass only considers primary-object canaries that already occur in the owner read F1. A per-field canary planted in P that F1 does not contain is skipped entirely, so its presence in F0/F2/F3 neither counts as a crossed field nor prevents `false`.

Frozen contract, `scourge.oracle-specifications.v1`, web.private-object-read.v1:
- `false`: "setup is valid and the primary canary is absent from F0, F2, and F3".
- exposure: "unauthenticated: the primary canary is present in F0 or F3".
- POR-03/POR-10: P carries fresh, distinct *per-field* canaries; "each declared field has its own canary and every crossed field is reported independently".
- INV-07: an invalid setup/measurement is never `false`.

Repro (saved-observation JSON, no code change):
1. Start from crates/scourge-verify/tests/fixtures/observations/false-no-exposure.json.
2. Append `{"field":"note","canary":"33333333333333333333333333333333"}` to flows[P].plant.canaries.
3. Set flows[F0].body to hex of `{"note":"3333...33"}` (or flows[F2].body for the cross-principal variant).
4. `evaluate` -> result=false, exposure=None, fields_crossed=[], reason_codes=[].

The same shape also downgrades a `true`: keep F1=A(label), set F2=A(label), and put B(note) in F0. Actual: result=true, exposure=CrossPrincipal, fields_crossed=["label"]. The primary canary B is present in F0, so the frozen exposure is `unauthenticated` and field "note" crossed.

Expected: `false` only when *no* primary canary occurs in F0/F2/F3. If a treatment read carries a primary canary that F1 did not establish, that is not `false`; it is at best `true` for that field (unauthenticated when it is in F0/F3) or, conservatively, `invalid` with OBSERVER_INVALID/EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE because the owner read did not confirm the field.

Impact: silent false negative for field-level exposure where the owner view masks or omits a declared field (the high-value field-authz case), plus undereported `fields_crossed` and a severity downgrade from unauthenticated to cross_principal. Existing tests all use one primary canary except `reporting_is_per_declared_field`, which puts both canaries in F1, so the gap is untested.

Fix: iterate all primary canaries for treatment matching; compute `false` from absence of every primary canary in F0/F2/F3; raise OBSERVER_INVALID/EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE for a treatment-only canary. Add a multi-field/partial-F1 test (mutating the fixture above is enough).

[MEDIUM] gzip/deflate decoding silently stops after the first member/stream

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/src/decode.rs:270-272 (`gunzip` uses `flate2::read::GzDecoder`) and :274-286 (`inflate` uses single-stream `ZlibDecoder`/`DeflateDecoder`).

`GzDecoder` reads only the first gzip member. RFC 1952 defines a gzip file as a series of members, and flate2's own docs point at `MultiGzDecoder` for all members. The zlib/raw-deflate path likewise accepts the first stream and ignores trailing bytes. No error is raised, so the saved body is silently truncated before canary matching.

Repro:
1. Build a two-member gzip body: `gzip(b"{\"label\":\"\"}") || gzip(b"{\"note\":\"<primary canary>\"}")`.
2. Set flows[F2].body to that hex, flows[F2].decoding = {transfer:"identity", content:"gzip", json_string_body:false}, flows[F2].decoder = "gzip" in crates/scourge-verify/tests/fixtures/observations/false-no-exposure.json.
3. `evaluate` -> result=false, no reason codes. Direct `decode` returns only the first member's bytes (12 in my probe).
A corrupt second member is also accepted silently.

Expected: matching runs over the decoded response body (bone, plan §6.5), so every member/stream must be decoded; or, if trailing data is unsupported, the decoder must return Truncated/Corrupt -> EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. It must not silently drop bytes.

Impact: a target that emits concatenated gzip members (valid HTTP) or uses that framing deliberately defeats the canary match and yields a `false` negative; POR-09's named/bounded decoding guarantee is not met for those bodies.

Fix: use `MultiGzDecoder` (or loop members) for gzip and reject non-empty trailing bytes after a zlib/raw-deflate stream; add a two-member test for both the positive (canary in member 2) and corrupt-member cases.

[LOW] `after_owner_read` is derived per canary and can be true although F0 already exposed a different field

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:506-508 (`if !in_first_read && in_anonymous_read { after_owner_read = true; }`).

Frozen exposure: "after_owner_read: F0 lacks the primary canary and F3 contains it". The implementation ORs the per-field condition: it returns true if *some* crossed canary is absent from F0 and present in F3, even when another primary canary is present in F0.

Repro: in false-no-exposure.json add a second field canary B to P; make F1 contain A and B; F0 contain A; F3 contain B. Actual: result=true, exposure=Unauthenticated (correct), after_owner_read=Some(true), fields_crossed=["label","note"]. F0 did carry a primary canary, so the round-level note should be false under the frozen wording; the exposure did not appear only after the owner read.

Impact: low - verdict and exposure are unaffected, but the note can overstate the cache-priming hypothesis (the F-37 shape) for a finding.

Fix: derive the round note as `no primary canary in F0 && some primary canary in F3`, or record per-field provenance in `fields_crossed`/a parallel structure and document the aggregate rule.

[LOW] `after_owner_read` is derived per canary and can be true although F0 already exposed a different field

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:506-508 (`if !in_first_read && in_anonymous_read { after_owner_read = true; }`).

Frozen exposure: "after_owner_read: F0 lacks the primary canary and F3 contains it". The implementation ORs the per-field condition: it returns true if *some* crossed canary is absent from F0 and present in F3, even when another primary canary is present in F0.

Repro: in false-no-exposure.json add a second field canary B to P; make F1 contain A and B; F0 contain A; F3 contain B. Actual: result=true, exposure=Unauthenticated (correct), after_owner_read=Some(true), fields_crossed=["label","note"]. F0 did carry a primary canary, so the round-level note should be false under the frozen wording; the exposure did not appear only after the owner read.

Impact: low - verdict and exposure are unaffected, but the note can overstate the cache-priming hypothesis (the F-37 shape) for a finding.

Fix: derive the round note as `no primary canary in F0 && some primary canary in F3`, or record per-field provenance in `fields_crossed`/a parallel structure and document the aggregate rule.

[LOW] Flow ordering is stricter than frozen POR-07 and turns back a complete, bound round

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:400-414 (strictly increasing `sequence` over all 12 flows in `FlowId::REQUIRED` order).

Frozen POR-07: "F0 precedes F1 and F3 follows it so after_owner_read is derived from the ordered pair". POR-08 requires every required flow to be present, complete and bound to this run; neither check freezes an order between I1/I2, P/P2, F2/F3, F4/I3/I4 or I4/C.

Repro (false-no-exposure.json):
- Set P2.sequence=3 and P.sequence=4 (plant the control object first). Actual: result=invalid, reason EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, evidence [FlowOrder { flow: P2, after: P }].
- Or swap F2.sequence=8 and F3.sequence=7 (F3 still follows F1 at 6). Actual: EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, FlowOrder { flow: F3, after: F2 }.
In both cases every flow is present, complete, run-bound and F0<F1<F3 holds.

Expected: a verdict (the frozen controls are satisfied). Impact: low - a false invalid that discards valid evidence; it never produces a wrong `true`/`false`. It can also reject records whose acquisition ticks tie.

Fix: check only the frozen relations (F0 < F1 < F3), or make the extra total order an explicit, tested requirement with a stated reason. `tests/por_checks.rs::por_07` only exercises F1 vs F0, so the extra constraint is not covered by the POR-07 test.

[LOW] POR-06 test claims superset rejection but only tests a prefix; first assignment is dead

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/tests/por_checks.rs:164-171.

Line 168 assigns `body_with(&common::primary())` and line 169 immediately overwrites it, so that write is dead. The comment says "Nor can a prefix or superset of the current canary", but only a 31-character prefix is tested. A body containing the 32-character canary inside a longer token (`<canary>ff`) is counted as crossed (verified with `evaluate`), which is the opposite of what the comment implies.

Impact: low - no wrong verdict is demonstrated (substring matching is a defensible reading of "occurs", and stale/global values remain different strings), but the mutation-kill claim for POR-06 is weaker than stated and the exact-match semantics are undocumented.

Fix: either add a real superset case and define token-boundary matching in `Canary::occurs_in` (observations.rs), or drop the superset claim and the dead assignment and document that matching is a byte-substring test.

[LOW] `json_string` decoder cannot decode the fixture `escaped_json` shape it is named for

Anchor: crates/scourge-verify/src/decode.rs:341-372 (`unescape_json_string` requires the whole body to be one JSON string literal) and the module doc at :10-13 ("application/json bodies that carry the real payload as an escaped string").

The referee fixture's `escaped_json` mode emits `{"document":"<escaped note JSON>"}` (fixtures/target/src/orders.rs:182-185; fixtures/target/referee/ground-truth.json response_modes.escaped_json expects canary "found"). Naming decoder `json_string` on that body returns DecodeError::Corrupt -> EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, i.e. invalid for a mode whose ground truth expects the canary found. The canary is still found with identity decoding because the 32-hex form survives escaping, so the mode passes only if the verifier does not name the decoder.

Repro: `decode(b"{\"document\":\"{\\\"note\\\":\\\"<canary>\\\"}\"}", Decoding { json_string_body: true, .. }, DecodeLimits::default())` -> Err(Corrupt); the same bytes with `json_string_body: false` decode and contain the canary.

Impact: low - only affects a verifier that names the decoder for this shape; but the doc comment and the decoder name invite exactly that, and there is no fixture-shaped test.

Fix: either support a nested/wrapper escaped string (e.g. find the single string member) or narrow the doc/decoder to top-level JSON string bodies, and add a test built from the fixture's escaped_json bytes.

Note for the review record: comment th-5jiysb.2 (after_owner_read per-canary derivation) is a separate LOW finding and is tracked as its own thread th-33yc3s. It is not part of this HIGH finding. There is no comment-deletion command, so this note records the split.

data.reason: BLOCK on fe96a694bbddac0feab1e3eb2c4fda1ec7f67ad4: 1 high, 1 medium, 4 low findings. HIGH th-5jiysb: false (and cross_principal) drop planted per-field canaries absent from F1, producing silent false negatives and exposure downgrade. MEDIUM th-16uz08: gzip/zlib decoding stops after the first member/stream and silently truncates the body. LOW: th-33yc3s after_owner_read aggregate; th-mocv1y ordering stricter than POR-07; th-16acoz POR-06 superset test gap; th-3u51lj json_string vs fixture escaped_json. All threads are open.

data.body: Fixed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c (workspace bn-20u, base 5009a9b). The exposure pass no longer skips a primary canary that F1 does not show: crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:502-529 now matches every planted primary canary in F0/F2/F3 independently, so a field F1 masked is reported, the exposure stays unauthenticated when that canary is in F0 or F3, and the round-level note is derived once. false now requires every primary canary to be absent from F0, F2 and F3 (oracle.rs:531-544). POR-04 is unchanged and round-level: an owner read showing no primary canary is still OBSERVER_INVALID, so the frozen precedence SAME_SUBJECT > OBSERVER_INVALID > CANARY_NOT_SPECIFIC > SESSION_DRIFT > EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE is untouched. No new reason code and no new oracle version. Evidence: tests/per_field.rs (8 tests) covers your reproducer and both variants - canary only in F0 => true/unauthenticated/fields [note] (was false), canary only in F2 => true/cross_principal, F1+F2 show label with note in F0 => unauthenticated (was the cross_principal downgrade), F1 empty of primary canaries with a treatment hit => OBSERVER_INVALID never false, plus false-requires-all and one-hit-blocks-false. A saved-document regression is crates/scourge-verify/tests/fixtures/observations/partial-f1-f0-field-exposure.json asserted by saved_observations.rs:241. Mutation probe: re-adding the continue-on-F1-absence makes 4 per_field tests fail. just check passes (scourge-verify 120 tests).

Fixed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c. gzip now uses flate2's MultiGzDecoder (crates/scourge-verify/src/decode.rs:323-325), so every RFC 1952 member is decoded into one buffer under one shared size/ratio bound over the whole body; a corrupt later member and trailing non-member bytes both surface as Corrupt/Truncated instead of a silent stop. For zlib/raw deflate (decode.rs:334-402), single_stream now compares the decoder's total_in with the saved body length and returns Corrupt when the stream ends early, so a second stream or trailing bytes are never dropped; a body with a valid zlib header (RFC 1950 CMF/FLG check) is decoded only as zlib and cannot be reinterpreted as raw deflate, and unheadered bodies fall back to raw deflate as before. Evidence in tests/decoding.rs: every_gzip_member_is_decoded_under_one_shared_bound (552), a_canary_in_the_second_gzip_member_is_found_by_the_oracle (567, your reproducer: canary in member 2 => true), a_corrupt_later_gzip_member_is_refused (587), gzip_bytes_that_are_not_another_member_are_refused (602), the_gzip_member_bound_is_shared_across_members (615: 10 bytes across members accepted at limit 10, OverLimit at 9), a_second_zlib_stream_is_refused (628), trailing_bytes_after_a_zlib_stream_are_refused (638), raw_deflate_trailing_bytes_are_refused (648), a_single_zlib_or_raw_deflate_stream_still_decodes (661) so the strictness did not break the supported single-stream modes. Mutation probes: reverting to GzDecoder fails 5 tests; removing the total_in check fails the 3 trailing/zlib-stream tests. Every failure is EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE (existing an_undecodable_flow test), never false.

Fixed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c. after_owner_read is now derived once per round as 'no primary canary occurs in F0 and at least one occurs in F3' (crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:519-529), replacing the per-canary OR at the old 506-508. The field doc (oracle.rs:184-187) and the module doc state the round-level rule. Evidence: tests/per_field.rs:142 after_owner_read_is_a_round_level_note_not_a_per_canary_one is exactly your reproducer (F1 shows label+note, F0 shows label, F3 shows note) and now asserts Some(false) with fields [label, note] and unauthenticated; tests/per_field.rs:123 asserts Some(true) for the partial-F1 case where only F3 carries a primary canary; outcomes.rs still pins true/false/unauthenticated/cross_principal notes. Mutation probe: replacing the aggregate with a per-canary/F3-only expression fails that test. Verdict and exposure are unchanged.

Fixed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c. The strictly-increasing-sequence loop over all twelve flows is gone. crates/scourge-verify/src/oracle.rs:408-430 enforces only the frozen POR-07 relations through one helper: after.sequence <= before.sequence for (F0, F1) and (F1, F3), reported as FlowOrder { flow: after, after: before }; the check is skipped when either body is undecodable so the round falls through to EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE as before. No order is frozen between I1/I2, P/P2, F2/F3, F4/I3/I4 or I4/C, and the comment states why (POR-08 freezes presence, completeness and run binding, not unrelated order). Evidence: tests/por_checks.rs:194 por_07_only_f0_before_f1_and_f1_before_f3_are_frozen asserts both frozen directions and the exact cause pairs; tests/por_checks.rs:235 por_07_freezes_no_order_between_unrelated_flows asserts your reproducers now conclude - control planted first (P2=3, P=4) => false with empty evidence; F2 and F3 sharing tick 8 => false; F0 and F2 tied => false; F2=8 with F3=7 (F3 still after F1=6) => false. Mutation probe: restoring the total-order loop fails both tests.

Fixed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c. The dead assignment is gone. tests/por_checks.rs:158 por_06_only_the_exact_current_primary_canary_counts now: (1) asserts a stale non-run canary in F2 stays false, (2) asserts a 31-character truncation of the current canary stays false, (3) asserts the documented byte-substring semantics explicitly - a body whose JSON string is <canary>ff is counted, because the 32 lowercase hex bytes were disclosed - and (4) asserts the exact current canary counts and the crossed field is reported. I did not implement a token-boundary rule: the frozen contract does not require one, so instead of claiming a superset rejection the code does not perform, Canary::occurs_in (observations.rs:265-278) now documents that matching is a byte-substring test with no token-boundary rule, what 'exact' means in POR-06 (the exact current run-minted value versus stale or truncated content), and why an ASCII embed still counts. The oracle comment at oracle.rs:502-506 repeats that. No claim of untested superset rejection remains in code or tests.

Fixed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c. unescape_json_string (crates/scourge-verify/src/decode.rs:469-484) now accepts exactly two strict shapes: a bare JSON string literal, and a one-member JSON object whose only member is a string - the fixture's {"document":"<escaped note>"} wrapper (decode_json_document_wrapper, decode.rs:486-506, with decode_json_string_literal at 508-548 unchanged in strictness). Parsing is still bounded and hand-rolled: one member only (a duplicate/second member, an empty object, a non-string value, an escaped-but-unterminated literal, control bytes, invalid escapes or lone surrogates, and any trailing bytes are Corrupt), output can never exceed the input, and no allocation is sized by a declared number. Decoder naming is therefore usable for this mode instead of returning EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE. Evidence: tests/decoding.rs:670 the_fixture_escaped_json_wrapper_decodes_to_the_document_with_the_canary builds the exact {"document": serde_json::to_string(note)} shape with the ground-truth note 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef and asserts the decoded document plus occurs_in; decoding.rs:703 the_oracle_finds_the_canary_through_the_fixture_escaped_json_shape names json_string on F2 and gets true; decoding.rs:395 covers the wrapped shape generally; decoding.rs:357 refuses the shapes that are not one document string. The doc comment and module doc now state both accepted shapes rather than implying the wrapper was supported. Mutation probe: removing the wrapper branch fails 3 tests.

Residual risk from the review, addressed at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c: record-supplied decode limits are untrusted, so decode() clamps them to compiled ceilings before any allocation (crates/scourge-verify/src/decode.rs:41-50 MAX_DECODED_BYTES_CEILING 16 MiB and MAX_EXPANSION_RATIO_CEILING 10000, DecodeLimits::clamped at :84, applied at :266). A document can narrow the bounds but never lift them, and no record, template or agent can raise the constant. Boundary evidence in tests/decoding.rs: a_record_cannot_request_more_than_the_compiled_decode_ceilings (721: u64::MAX both fields clamps to the ceilings, at-ceiling kept, one-below kept, DEFAULT already inside), an_unbounded_record_limit_still_stops_at_the_compiled_ceiling (760: gzip of ceiling+1 bytes with u64::MAX limits => OverLimit) and an_identity_body_at_the_compiled_ceiling_is_accepted_and_one_byte_over_is_refused (773). Mutation probe: deleting the clamp fails both dynamic tests. Unsupported codings stay typed and closed: ContentCoding/TransferCoding are exhaustive serde enums with deny_unknown_fields, asserted by saved_observations.rs:195 an_unsupported_coding_is_rejected_as_typed_input (br, 'gzip, br', 'GZIP', transfer gzip, extra decoding key) and :221 the_typed_coding_enums_are_closed. No status or policy input was added: the oracle signature is unchanged, evaluate(&SavedObservations) -> Evaluation, and the existing status/policy boundary tests still pass. No network, credentials, target interaction, instrument adapter or dispatch was added.

Anchor index for the rereview at aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c (the replies above cite a few line ranges loosely; these are the exact ones): oracle.rs:408-430 frozen F0<F1<F3 ordering only, :444-452 round-level POR-04 OBSERVER_INVALID, :502-526 per-field treatment matching (no F1 gate), :527-529 round-level after_owner_read, :531-543 false only when every primary canary is out of F0/F2/F3, :545-560 true/exposure; observations.rs:199-207 Canary::occurs_in byte-substring doc; decode.rs:41-50 compiled ceilings, :84-96 DecodeLimits::clamped, :266 clamp before allocation, :323-325 MultiGzDecoder, :334-402 zlib/raw-deflate single-stream + trailing rejection, :469-483 unescape_json_string, :486-505 one-member document wrapper, :508-547 strict string-literal decoder.

Record note: the trailing 'Exact commit: fe96a694...' in the review description is the original request text; after retarget the review's authoritative target is aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c over base 5009a9b6ec79e881a3c34d59ad7454019eeb8485, which is the HEAD in workspace bn-20u and the commit these replies describe. The 6 finding threads were left open for the reviewer to resolve.

[verified aeba762] Reproduced independently at exact HEAD aeba76239636c0596cd6ab5cae686c409cc0fd3c (base 5009a9b) with a read-only probe crate outside the workspace driving only public APIs: 136 assertions, 0 failures.

- Your HIGH reproducer now concludes true / unauthenticated / fields ["note"] (P carries label+note, F1 shows only label, F0 carries note). The F2 variant concludes true / cross_principal / ["note"].
- The severity-downgrade variant (F1 label, F2 label, F0 note) is unauthenticated with fields ["label","note"], not cross_principal.
- Three fields split across the treatments report all three (["hash","label","note"]); after_owner_read is false there because F0 carried a primary canary.
- false now requires every primary canary absent: F1 carrying both canaries with stale-only treatments stays false; one treatment hit blocks false for every other field.
- POR-04 is still round-level: F1 showing only the control canary while the note canary is in F0/F2/F3 is invalid / OBSERVER_INVALID (after_owner_read None), never false.
- Duplicate per-field canaries or duplicate field names stay EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, never false.
- The saved-document regression partial-f1-f0-field-exposure.json is honest: P canaries label=1111…/note=3333…, F1 shows only label, F0 shows note.

Mutation probes on a copy of the tree: re-adding the F1-absence `continue` fails 5 tests (4 in tests/per_field.rs plus saved_observations.rs::a_saved_round_whose_f1_masked_a_field_still_reports_the_f0_exposure); deriving false from primary.first() only fails 6 tests. Verdict, exposure and fields_crossed are unchanged by the round-level note. Resolving.

[verified aeba762] Reproduced at aeba762 with my own codec vectors; every point holds.

- MultiGzDecoder: a canary in the second member is decoded and found by the oracle (true, field label); 5000 tiny members decode (105000 coded -> 5000 decoded).
- A corrupt second member and a corrupt third member are Corrupt; trailing non-member bytes are Corrupt; gzip followed by a truncated gzip header is Truncated; trailing zero padding is refused (Truncated) - conservative, and it is a silent-truncation fix rather than a new silent drop.
- Shared bound: two members of 5 bytes each decode at limit 10 and are OverLimit at 9.
- zlib + second stream, zlib + trailing bytes and raw deflate + trailing bytes are all Corrupt; a single zlib / raw deflate / gzip stream still decodes.
- Exact-length accounting is clean: zlib and raw deflate round-trip for payload sizes 0..=300 and 512/1024/4096/65535/1000000 with zero false-invalids, and ZlibDecoder total_in == body length for a valid zlib stream (15/15), i.e. the type check does not reject honest bodies.
- chunked + multi-member gzip decodes correctly.
- Every refusal surfaces as EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE (invalid), never false.
Mutation probes: switching back to GzDecoder fails 5 tests (exactly the five gzip tests); dropping the total_in comparison fails the 3 trailing/second-stream tests.

One accepted residual risk from this design, recorded separately and not blocking: has_zlib_header takes precedence, so a legal raw-deflate stored block whose first two bytes happen to be 78 9c is refused instead of falling back to raw deflate. Direction is invalid, never a wrong true/false, and a target can force invalid with any corruption. Resolving.

[verified aeba762] The aggregate is now round-level and matches the frozen wording "F0 lacks the primary canary and F3 contains it".

Independent probes:
- F0 carries nothing, F3 carries a primary canary -> Some(true).
- Your reproducer (F1 label+note, F0 label, F3 note) -> true / unauthenticated / fields ["label","note"] / Some(false).
- F0-only -> Some(false); F2-only -> Some(false); false verdict -> Some(false); invalid -> None.
Mutation: replacing the aggregate with the old per-canary OR, or with a plain F3-only expression, fails tests/per_field.rs::after_owner_read_is_a_round_level_note_not_a_per_canary_one. Verdict and exposure are unaffected in every case. Resolving.

[verified aeba762] Only the frozen POR-07 relations are enforced now, and I confirmed both directions.

Conclusive (no evidence) at aeba762: P2 before P (3/4); F2=8 with F3=7 while F3 still follows F1=6; F2/F3 on one tick; F0/F2 on one tick; and a fully scrambled round (I1=12, I2=11, P=9, P2=7, F0=1, F1=2, F2=8, F3=3, F4=10, I3=6, I4=5, C=4) that satisfies only F0<F1<F3.
Invalid: F1 tied with F0 -> FlowOrder{flow:F1, after:F0}; F1 before F0; F3 tied with F1 -> FlowOrder{flow:F3, after:F1}; F3 before F1; all twelve on one tick -> exactly two causes (the two frozen pairs).
The check is still skipped when either body is unusable: a tied F0/F1 with a partial F0 body yields only the completeness cause.
Mutation: restoring the strictly-increasing loop over FlowId::REQUIRED fails both por_07 tests. Resolving.

[verified aeba762] The dead assignment is gone and the semantics are now pinned honestly.

A legal RFC 1951 stored block may set the five "ignored" bits after BFINAL/BTYPE, so a hand-built raw-deflate body can begin 78 9c. Concrete vector: 78 9c | LEN=0x009c | NLEN | 156 stored bytes | final empty block. A plain raw-deflate decoder returns the document containing the canary; decode(..., content: Deflate) returns Corrupt because ZlibDecoder fails and the raw fallback is skipped. Impact: crafted or very unusual framing turns a possible true into invalid; a target able to control response bytes can already force invalid with any corruption, so this adds no capability and the direction is conservative. The code comment states the precedence honestly. A body ending in 0 CRLF CRLF followed by a canary-bearing tail decodes to the pre-terminator payload with no error. This is pre-existing (unchanged by aeba762) and outside th-16uz08 gzip/zlib scope; a chunked HTTP message ends at the terminator, so the bytes belong to no named coding.
